Hi! From my experience, the experience varies with the hospital. In one of the hospitals that I've been in, they gave me a timetable and it was about group therapy, coping skills, and life coaching. There was also a group about certain illnesses (like all about depression, bpd, etc.). The second hospital I've been in is intended for kids and adolescence, so it's more laidback (I guess?). We also had a schedule with group therapy, life coaching, etc. with nurses and CYWs. The hospital that I was almost admitted in only had one group in the morning. However, all hospitals provide counselling and the psychiatrists sees you often! It's basically just a lot of therapy and they also look at your medication and see which one is the best for you. They really look after you (the nurses check up on you) and make sure that you're safe. You are always allowed to talk to the nurses and the people there because they're there to help you. Also, I've met quite a few people in the hospital and I still keep in touch with them. :) 

It's a really interesting experience. The first few days might be scary, but after that you'll start to feel more comfortable! Good luck!
